results.reason: The response computes the August 16, 2026 deadline and says it passed before signing. It cites Schedule 3.12's 'intends to deliver' language, signalling the notice has not been delivered. It explains expiry on November 14, 2026, before the November 30 closing, and flags that the Section 3.12(c) 'through November 2029' representation is inaccurate, exposing sellers to an indemnification claim.

The response identifies the 100% sale as a Change of Control under Section 1.3(a), with consent required under Section 14.2 and a termination right under Section 14.3. It notes Velloran's consent is not on Schedule 3.6 and so falls outside Sections 6.4 and 7.1(d). It recommends adding the consent and starting the request immediately.

The response identifies the six-state versus four-state mismatch and the 18-month post-term restriction, and recommends narrowing the Side Letter territory. However, it never explains that the expanded definition controls under the Section 19.4 order of precedence. Section 19.4 is cited only in the governing-law issue and is not tied to the Territory definition.

The response identifies New York law and New York County courts versus Delaware law and Wilmington courts. It explains the risk of conflicts and inconsistent treatment of the interlinked agreements. It recommends a conforming amendment to align governing law and forum.
The response states the Initial Term ends November 14, 2026.
The response states the Target Closing Date is November 30, 2026.
The response states the Distribution Agreement Territory is Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey and Pennsylvania only.
The memo is addressed to the Partner, and each issue lists documents and sections, why it matters, and a recommended fix.
The most significant issues come first, Issues 1 and 2 carry explicit flags to raise with the client and Quillon's counsel, and a priority table is included.

Renewal is discussed only conditionally ('if properly delivered'). The response notes that delivery before Closing would be after the deadline, and never concludes the agreement renewed or that timely notice remains possible.
The response expressly states Velloran's consent is not on Schedule 3.6 and not a closing condition.
